title: Compatible finite-stage units and counits descend to an adjunction
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, S and T stage systems on C_i and D_i, and F:S.Morphism T and G:T.Morphism S coherent morphisms. Suppose adjunctions a_i:F.Phi_i left-adjoint G.Phi_i are given. Suppose their units form a compatible morphism from the identity stage-system morphism to F.comp G, and their counits a compatible morphism from G.comp F to the identity. Then the induced pair functors F.functor and G.functor are adjoint. Their unit and counit at (i,x) are precisely the inclusions of the finite unit and counit, through the canonical identity-component composition comparisons.

proof.text: Descend each compatible family with Morphism.descNatTrans. Compose with functorIdIso and functorCompIso to give transformations of the required functors.

At an object (i,x) both comparison isomorphisms have identity components. Functor_map_iota identifies the image of the descended unit under F with the inclusion of F_i applied to the finite unit. Its composite with the descended counit is therefore the inclusion of the finite left triangle, hence the identity. The right triangle is identical with G in place of F. These transformations and the two equations construct the adjunction.
